articles.detail: 5 cycles, 4 completed at snapshot, avg 8/cycle (62 yesterday)

experiment: Skipped — every goal metric clears its target, no experiment is active, and no pause gate is set. The one persistent weakness, single-source science and tech, was shown by the 2026-05-09 floor experiment to be capped by feed supply rather than by any selector parameter, so spending the slot on the tunable surface would not reach it.
weakestArea: Multi-source depth remains concentrated in politics and economy: of the 47 articles committed so far today, politics ran 6 of 16 multi-source and economy 5 of 12, while science managed 1 of 9 and tech 1 of 10. That is a real improvement on yesterday, when science had none, but a fifth of daily output still rests on a single outlet each. Regional balance also skewed: the Americas took 21 of 62 (34%) against 14 yesterday, and Oceania fell to a single article.
watching: The Iran war has crossed into economic warfare: Hormuz strikes resumed, a rename was floated from Washington, tanker-for-tanker policy was adopted, and the oil shock is now cited against a Fed cut — four datelines describing one transmission chain.
Russia is being sourced into Iran's missile programme at the same time as US labs are reported arming Israel quietly, which puts both patrons on the record within a single day.
Sudan produced three separate arcs — the African Union backing rejected, an airstrike on a UN convoy, and a Dilling dateline — while Radio Dabanga carried two of them alone.

AI industry consolidation and fragility landed together: Nvidia buying Hugging Face, simultaneous outages across the major providers, Google shipping a cyber model, and ASEAN writing rules around all of it.
Nepal appears twice from opposite ends of the same flood — a warning system that failed and a corridor now shut — which is a follow-through worth keeping paired.
coverageGaps: Oceania recorded one article (Brisbane) and the Pacific Islands are again unrepresented, a third consecutive day at or below two.
Science ran nine articles with one multi-source story; the sourcing cluster cannot lift while the category is structurally single-outlet.
The metrics file again lists general-desk outlets — Mirror, Albanian Daily News, The National — among science sources, which suggests the science tag is being applied to non-specialist copy.
Latin America improved on yesterday with Caracas and Trujillo datelines, but Bolivia and Venezuela still arrive mainly through US-facing framings.
Central Asia surfaced only through Kazakhstan charging a scholar; no economic or energy coverage from the region despite the oil story running all day.
context: Output held at 62 for a second day across five cycles averaging 1443s (selector 283s, writer 275s, editor 112s) — the slowest daily average this week, though every stage sat far inside its timeout and the fifth cycle was still publishing when metrics were taken. Unique sources recovered sharply from 44 to 62, so concentration reversed yesterday's drift and no outlet exceeds 10%. Freshness stayed strong at a 0.3 median but is computed on 16 dated articles of 62, a thin sample. Duplicates held at zero for a sixth day. All datelines today are cities, so yesterday's non-city dateline problem did not recur. No experiment has run since May, and the reason is unchanged.
